P1.evidence: Application read back and used to open warmly and specifically — 'I read briefly through the application again... So now you're down to 215, 225, somewhere between there, right?' Real rapport was built over the prospect's car wheels. Frame agreement asked and given: 'Does that all sound good?' 'Yeah, absolutely.' Open question run properly: 'walk me through it, dude. Like, what do you feel we could potentially help you with?' Frame three-part as always — 'where you're at, where you're trying to get to, what's missing in between'.

P2.evidence: Baseline was effectively not run, and on this prospect that is the whole finding. Age was never asked. Height appeared only because the prospect used it himself. Health conditions were never asked — ankylosing spondylitis, an umbilical hernia, two shoulder surgeries, raised cholesterol and triglycerides and schizoaffective disorder were every one of them volunteered, which the spec scores as a miss because the script credits asking. Injuries and movement limitations likewise never asked. Most striking of all, the current training week was never established: a six-month training programme was sold without the rep ever finding out what the man does now. Diet was asked, but as an afterthought twenty-eight minutes in and mid-presentation — 'I forgot to ask, how's your diet as a whole?' — and it did produce useful detail. Sleep and daytime energy both skipped, on a prospect who volunteered that he cannot breathe and takes an hour each morning to mobilise his back.

P3.evidence: The bridge ran twice and ran well — 'what's the motivation behind making this change, man?' and later 'what's the drive behind all this stuff for you?' — and one genuinely good challenge landed: told he would never get his wrestling physique back, the rep asked 'Why not?' and then 'if you could get to some semblance of a wrestling physique, do you think you'd want to do that?' 'Absolutely.' The deepest material in the entire batch then arrived, almost all of it self-supplied: purpose, self-reliance, the nine noble virtues, isolation, a brother's suicide. What the rep did not do is direct any of it. 'Who else does that impact?' was never asked of a man who is his mother's full-time carer. Mobility, strength and energy were never offered as goal alternatives. Nothing was reflected back. The prospect did the work of the phase himself.

P4.evidence: The gap was surfaced cleanly with a well-framed question — 'Why are we feeling like we might need a little bit of help to get that 30 pounds, man?' — and the prospect named it himself twice: 'the biggest thing is just having the accountability, having some sort of outside motivation' and later 'I don't have anyone to hold me accountable.' Past attempts came out only as narrative, never as a question: the push-ups and sit-ups with his ex, stopped by the hernia. Why it did not stick was never asked and neither was the root-cause move, which matters because the prospect's own theory — ADHD and no external structure — was sitting there to be tested.

P5.evidence: The two-year question was asked properly and pressed once when the first answer deflected. It still came back deflected — 'I'll figure something else out... I'm very adaptable' — with a friend and martial arts as the alternative. The rep accepted it: 'Sure. Makes sense.' No settle question, no 'why not', no line in the sand. This is the third call in the batch where the consequence frame was raised, answered away and abandoned, and it is the most costly instance because the real consequence was already on the table in the prospect's own words: 'If I stop, then I'm done.'

P6.evidence: The best-executed commitment check in the batch and correctly placed before the price. The belief question was framed as a score and then probed — 'if you had rate everything we talked about, 1 to 10... just putting the finances aside, where would you say you're at?' answered '10', followed by 'What stood out to you the most?' and 'why did that stand out to you the most?' The all-in question was asked in full and answered 'Yes.' P6c is partial only because when hesitation surfaced at the price the script says return to Phase 5, and the rep went into the money play instead.

P11.evidence: A close was attempted but no agreement was reached, so payment, onboarding, agreement signature and welcome steps were all unreachable. The call ended on a weekly text follow-up rather than a transaction.

objection_plays.detail: The most complete open-wallet in the batch, run close to verbatim. Isolation first: 'finances aside, is there anything else at all that's keeping you from being less than 100% certain that this is the right thing and now is the right time?' Then the should-versus-how reframe: 'So we're not in like a should I, not in a should I do this where we're going back and forth on if this is right. literally how do we make [it work].' Then the break-it-up framing and the permission question in full: 'Are you willing to have an open and honest conversation about where you're at financially and we can figure out a plan?' The financial picture was then harvested properly — monthly income, an itemised expense breakdown, month-end surplus, credit score and history, number of credit lines and available credit on each. Only investments were skipped, and given what the numbers showed that is immaterial. Scored a hit on execution, and the execution is precisely what makes the next entry a finding.

SCRIPT GAP — THE MONEY PLAY HAS NO STOPPING RULE. Objection C tells the rep how to extract the financial picture and says nothing about what to do when the picture says no. Here it produced an unambiguous answer: $2,500 a month in, roughly $300 left at month end, $300 of total available credit, a credit score already dropping, and a man explicitly working with recovery and credit union programmes to stabilise his debts. Both options then offered exceed that surplus by two to four times — '$600, 700 bucks a month' on third-party finance the rep conceded he probably would not qualify for, and '$1,200 a month over six months' in house. The rep also asked about the credit union loan and offered to improvise further: 'I'm happy to do some weird custom thing if we need to.' Nothing in the playbook instructs a rep to stop, and nothing here did.

SCRIPT GAP — CLINICAL FIT, AT ITS MOST ACUTE. Ankylosing spondylitis fusing the spine, an umbilical hernia that protrudes under abdominal loading, two reconstructed shoulders, raised lipids, and schizoaffective disorder with an ADHD comorbidity. There is no screening step, no contraindication list, no clearance requirement and no referral path anywhere in the process. The rep did the opposite of screening — he offered the mobility work as treatment for the autoimmune condition and the programme as a plausible route out of serious depression.

'Worst case scenario, I'm going to start stacking some money away' is a timing deferral in substance, arriving in the last thirty seconds. No part of the play ran — no 'when does it actually become the right time', no cost-of-delay frame. It was accepted and converted into a weekly follow-up instead.
No think-about-it trigger; the prospect wanted it and said so, rating it a 10.
No partner involved; the prospect lives alone since his ex left.
No fear or doubt about the programme. If anything the risk ran the other way — belief was total.

notes: Two halves that point in opposite directions. The close itself was the most technically correct work in the batch: a proper 1-10 belief check, a genuine all-in commitment secured before price, and a textbook open-wallet. The discovery underneath it barely happened — no age, no health question, no injury question, and no idea what the man currently does for training, on a prospect with a spine-fusing autoimmune disease, a protruding hernia and two rebuilt shoulders who disclosed all of it unprompted. The coaching point is not technique. It is that both of the process failures here — no clinical gate and no affordability stopping rule — are missing from the script rather than from the rep, and this is the call where both of them cost the most.
